name: build_linear_contact_waypoints
summary: Build arm-independent TCP waypoint variants for a straight surface-normal contact task.

generality.rationale: Reusable TCP-origin geometry, but physical contact features and aperture-dependent offsets are absent; cross-task press transfer is unvalidated.
assumptions: A straight surface-normal sequence is appropriate and TCP-origin targeting suits the intended contact feature.
limitations: Does not model a finger/pad contact feature or aperture-dependent offset.
Does not select a manipulator, solve IK, check collision, execute motion, or cover grasp/place semantics.
tested_tasks: robotwin/press-stapler-aloha-agilex (geometry behavior preserved from harness_v2 iterations)

level.rationale: Deterministically derives four short TCP-pose sequences from measured point-normal contact geometry.

provenance.failure_gap: Linear-contact geometry was inseparably coupled to multi-arm selection and IK, preventing reuse of arm selection for grasp and place tasks.
evidence: plan_reachable_linear_contact mixed contact-specific waypoint construction with generic manipulator reachability search.
